kevin: Quick heads-up — ran the nightly batcher profiling with prefix cache enabled. Seeing an unexpected drop in avg tokens-per-batch (~30%) when cache-hit rate > 60%. Flamegraphs + kernel traces attached, but want eyes. Anyone seen this pattern?

marta: :eyes: Can you paste the short perf summary? Which kernel was chosen (int8/fp16/fallback)?

kevin: Small excerpt from the trace:```kernel: conv_attn_opt_v2
seq_len=128
batch_tokens_before=10240
batch_tokens_after=7140
cache_hit_rate=0.66
chosen_kernel=kv_fused_attn_int8
fallbacks=0
latency_p50:+12%```Seems like batcher is forming smaller batches when many requests are cache-hits.

arian: Interesting — my hunch: cache-hit-aware packing is aggressively admitting hits into fast-path which reduces the token-budget diversity inside the admission window. That changes the seq_len distribution the kernel selector sees -> it picks a kernel optimized for smaller work per-CU, so total throughput drops.

nora: I saw a similar blip on the canary yesterday. Our prefetcher marks some requests as 'hot' and batcher short-circuits waiting for more tokens to avoid latency for those users. That helps tail latency per-hot-rt but kills overall batching for mixed traffic.

marta: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) lower the eager-admit threshold for cache-hit fast-path (so hits don't immediately get their own tiny batches), or 2) add a small "staleness window" (e.g., 10-30ms) before hits are eligible for the fast-path packing. We should A/B and measure batch_tokens, p95 and kernel-switch rate.

kevin: Agree. Running a canary now: set cache-aware admit from 0.90 -> 0.75 and token_budget_target from 12k -> 9k on r3 pool. Will report perf-bot metrics shortly.

perf-bot: perf-bot: experiment started on r3-spot-2. Run id: exp-2026-03-17-01. Monitoring metrics: batch_tokens, p95_latency, kernel_switches_per_min.

arian: Please add a counter for "kernel-switch events per-minute" in the selector. If kernel switches spike when cache_hit_ratio rises, that's our correlation.

nora: Also log per-batch prefix-length distribution. If we see many tiny prefixes per-batch (<=8 tokens) that's the smoking gun that cache-hit packing is fragmenting batches.

kevin: Good call. I'll wire those logs and bump the canary now. If numbers look better, we should add a preset policy in Redwood Optimize: "cache-aware conservative" that sets admit thresholds and staleness defaults.

marta: @arian can you own the kernel-switch counter? @kevin ping me with the summary once perf-bot finishes. :thumbsup:

arian: On it — patching kernel selector hooks and adding the metric. Will post a short follow-up once the metric stream is live.

kevin: Thanks all — will dump the full flamegraphs + sample batch payloads once canary completes.
